problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable convex function on ℝⁿ with globally L-Lipschitz gradient. A global minimizer x⋆ exists with ‖x₀−x⋆‖≤R.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact binary comparison oracle: querying (x,y) returns whether f(x)≤f(y), including true on equality. No function values or gradients are supplied. Replies are fixed independently of history and seeds.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean space ℝⁿ with n≥1. Parameters n,L,R,ε,x₀ are public, with L,R,ε>0; the objective and minimizer are hidden.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The returned point must satisfy f(output)−f(x⋆)≤ε for a global minimizer x⋆.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The objective-gap guarantee holds almost surely over the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, within the supplied fixed comparison-query budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The smooth convex objective class is standard, but access is restricted to exact binary comparisons, with an almost-sure guarantee under a fixed query budget.

descriptionHtml:
Comparison-Based Smooth Convex Minimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable convex function f:Rn→R, where n≥1 is an integer. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz in the Euclidean norm, with L>0, and a given starting point x0∈Rn lies within distance R>0 of a global minimizer x⋆. At a queried pair (x,y), the oracle returns the Boolean value of f(x)≤f(y). For a tolerance ε>0, the goal is an output x¯∈Rn satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely under P, the law of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Rnf(x). Throughout, ∥⋅∥ denotes the Euclidean norm. The algorithm receives n, L, R, ε, and x0.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity). For every x,y∈Rn and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y).

Assumption 2 (Smoothness). The function f is differentiable everywhere on Rn, and its gradient satisfies ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥,x,y∈Rn.

Assumption 3 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈Rn such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈Rn,∥x0−x⋆∥≤R.

Queries may use any pair (x,y)∈Rn×Rn. Comparisons are exact: the reply is true precisely when f(x)≤f(y), including equality, and false otherwise.

After the allotted comparison calls, the output must satisfy f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤εP-a.s. The minimizer is fixed independently of the algorithm’s randomness; all global minimizers have the same objective value.

comparisonHtml:
Convex differentiable f:Rn→R, n≥1, with L-Lipschitz gradient and a minimizer x⋆ satisfying ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R; L,R,ε>0. The oracle returns 1[f(x)≤f(y)]. Target: f(xout)−f(x⋆)≤ε almost surely; (1) is deterministic and uses the public n,L,R,ε,x0.

Exact-comparison smooth convex optimization: ComparisonSmoothConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) ComparisonOrthConvex (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O((1+T)(nℓ+ℓ3)) comparisons
(2) Comparison-AdaNGD (Zhang and Li 2024, Thm. 2) O(n(1+T)ℓ) comparisons (1): T instead of T for T≥1, n≥ℓ2; last iterate instead of comparison-selected best iterate. (1) adds O((1+T)ℓ3) search overhead.
(3) Comparison cutting plane (Zhang and Li 2024, Thm. 3) O(n2ℓ) comparisons (1): gain n/T when 1≤T<n2, n≥ℓ2. At T=n: O(n3/2log⁡n) versus O(n2log⁡n). (1) loses T/n for T>n2; polynomial rather than logarithmic accuracy dependence.
(4) OrderACDM (Lobanov et al. 2024, Thm. 4.1); μ-strongly convex restriction O(nL/μ[1+log+⁡(LR2/ε)]Cls) comparisons, uniform coordinate bounds; expected accuracy (1): scope extends to μ=0; deterministic instead of expected accuracy. Rates are not comparable at μ=0. (1) lacks linear convergence for μ>0 and coordinate-smoothness gains on anisotropic instances.
(5) (Wu et al. 2026, Thm. 3.3); unique-minimizer restriction O(nT) exact values, T≥1; queries in B(x0,2R), output in B(x0,R) (1) uses comparisons instead of values on the common unique-minimizer class. (1) adds logarithmic factors and O(Tℓ3) overhead; no bounded-query guarantee.

Abbr: T=LR2/ε; ℓ=1+log⁡(n(1+T)); log+⁡u=max{0,log⁡u}; μ>0 is the strong-convexity modulus. Cls is the comparison cost of the line searches per OrderACDM iteration (logarithmic precision dependence, suppressed in its published oracle bound).

Wu, Wendao, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, et al. 2026. Near-Optimal Deterministic Exact-Value Complexity for Smooth Convex Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2609.18230.
Zhang, Chenyi, and Tongyang Li. 2024. Comparisons Are All You Need for Optimizing Smooth Functions. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2405.11454.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2

namespace LongTails.Setups.ComparisonSmoothConvex

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Point (n : ℕ) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)

structure Params where
  n : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : Point n

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance p := Point p.n → ℝ
  Query p := Point p.n × Point p.n
  Reply _ := Bool
  Output p := Point p.n
  publicInput p := p
  valid q := 1 ≤ q.n ∧ 0 < q.L ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, ‖gradient f x - gradient f y‖ ≤ q.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R) ∧
    (∀ history query seed, O.answer history query seed = decide (f query.2.1 ≤ f query.2.2))
  successful q f output P :=
    ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : MeasureTheory.Measure _), f (output ω) - f xstar ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.ComparisonSmoothConvex
